title: Chapter 1 Boss: Your Place in the Universe
objective: After this level you can trace Earth's address from our planet all the way out to the observable universe.
summary: The Milky Way is ~100,000 light-years across, Andromeda is ~2.5 million light-years away, and the observable universe holds billions of galaxies in a ~13.8-billion-year-old cosmos.

cards.headline: Chapter 1 finale. Let's zoom all the way out.
cards.body: Everything from Levels 1–9 was your neighborhood. Now for the city, the country and the planet.

cards.headline: Our galaxy
cards.body: The Milky Way is about 100,000 light-years across. Light from one edge would take 100,000 years to reach the other.

cards.fact: Andromeda, the nearest large spiral galaxy, is about 2.5 million light-years away.
cards.context: On a dark night you can see it with the naked eye as a faint smudge — the most distant thing most people will ever see unaided.

cards.headline: And then everything else
cards.body: The observable universe holds billions of galaxies, each with billions of stars. The universe itself is about 13.8 billion years old.

cards.headline: Chapter 1 complete
learned: The Milky Way is about 100,000 light-years across
Andromeda is about 2.5 million light-years away
The observable universe holds billions of galaxies
The universe is about 13.8 billion years old

questions.prompt: From Level 1: which galaxy is the Sun part of?

options.label: Andromeda
options.rationale: Andromeda is our neighbor, not our home.

options.label: The Large Magellanic Cloud
options.rationale: That's a small satellite galaxy of the Milky Way.

options.label: The solar system
options.rationale: The solar system is inside a galaxy, not a galaxy itself.

questions.explanation: The Sun is one of at least 100 billion stars in the Milky Way.

questions.prompt: About how old is the universe?

options.label: 100,000 years
options.rationale: That's roughly the Milky Way's width in light-years.

options.label: 4.6 billion years
options.rationale: That's the age of the Sun.

questions.explanation: The universe is about 13.8 billion years old — about three times older than the Sun.

questions.prompt: From Level 8: Andromeda is 2.5 million light-years away. What does that mean?

options.label: It takes 2.5 million years to fly there
options.rationale: No spacecraft goes anywhere near light speed.

options.label: It's 2.5 million km away
options.rationale: A light-year is about 9.46 trillion km.

options.label: Its light has traveled 2.5 million years to reach us

questions.explanation: A light-year is a distance; Andromeda's light has been traveling for about 2.5 million years.
